LESSON: WRITING 6.4.1 SPELLING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Writing 6.4.1 Spelling
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.4.1 Spelling, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we learn to spell words or names?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.4.1 Spelling together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: writing skills as the learner writes clearly and spells words correctly from a signed dictation.

Values

Unity: Cooperation as learner collaborates with peers as they form words related to the theme using letters of their names.

Link to

Values:
Unity: Cooperation as learner collaborates with peers as they form words related to the theme using letters of their names.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skill: Effective communication is enhanced as they spell words correctly in a signed dictation.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner is able to relate correct spelling of words to their learning in Kenya Sign Language

7.2.1

Fluency

(2 Lessons )

By the end of the sub strand, the

learner should be able to:

a)identify signed words with the

target letter- sound combinations

nd’ ‘nk’ and words ending with

‘ar’ in preparation for reading,

b) sign read a text accurately, at

the right speed, displaying the

right feelings and emotions for

fluency,

c) endorse sign reading simple,

short narratives and

informational texts in a variety

of genres.

● In pairs, learners are guided to

pick out, fingerspell and sign

words with letter sound

combinations ‘nd’ ‘nk’ and

words ending with ‘ar’ as in car,

far from a text.

● In pairs, learners are guided to

sign read words containing the

target letter- sound

combinations.

● In groups, learners are guided to

practise sign reading a text

repetitively and in unison.

● Individually, learner is guided to

engage in timed sign reading,

displaying the right facial

expressions and feelings making

appropriate pauses at punctuations.

● In pairs, learners are guided to

practise sign reading sentences

containing decodable and non- decodable words.

● In pairs, learners are guided to

recite a poem/sign sing songs

featuring the target words, for

example, injury, witness, bump,

survive, evade, careless, hurt,

hand cart, scar, tanker, accident,

speed, drive, traffic, road signs,

Reading

Comprehension

(2 lesson
s) By the end of the sub strand, the

learner should be able to:


a) recognise signs of vocabulary

related to the theme for

effective communication,


b) describe the characters and

events in the text to show

comprehension,


c) sign vocabulary related to the

theme for comprehension,


d) make predictions about a story

based on the title and picture,


e) respond to direct and indirect

questions in short simple

sentences to show

comprehension,


f) adopt reading pictures and

texts for enjoyment and

information.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to

watch a captioned video clip

or observe a signed

demonstration of vocabulary

related to accidents.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to

identify, fingerspell and sign

vocabulary related to

accidents.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to

look at the title and pictures in the

text to make predictions.


  -  In groups, learners are

guided to discuss as they

sign the setting and the

characters in the story.


  -  Individually, learner is

guided to sign read a text

related to theme and

respond to direct questions.


  -  Individually, learner is guided

to respond to indirect

questions using contextual

clues.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to

retell by signing a story with

peers.


  -  In pairs, learners are guided to role

play scenarios from the story.

1. How can you tell

what will happen in

this story?

2. What do the

pictures tell us

about the story?

77


  -  Individually, learner is guided

to talk as they sign about their

own experiences in relation to

the story.

Core Competencies to be developed:


  -  Communication and collaboration: Speaking and signing skills as the learner retells the story clearly and effectively with peers


  -  Creativity and imagination: Making connections as the learner link between the story and their own experiences.

Values:

Responsibility: Hardwork as the learner takes up roles as they role play scenarios from the story in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

Life skills: Self-esteem as the learner responds to comprehension questions correctly.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner is able to relate sign reading comprehension to other learning areas in Kiswahili Language Activities and Kenyan Sign Language.
